title: sync's foreign-session refusal names no override for a session that no longer exists
goal: When kbgit.py sync --push refuses commits made by another Claude session, its message says how to push them when that session is gone (a restarted or resumed orchestrator landing its own earlier work/<id> commits): --session <its Claude-Session url> or KB_SESSION, so the refusal is never a dead end; a TestSyncForeignSession test asserts the refusal names the override. Found by the SP-x2pvljz6 review (F3, ST-huvwo6cj).

run: import pathlib,sys; s=pathlib.Path('_tools/kbgit.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8'); i=s.index('were made by another Claude session'); sys.exit(0 if '--session' in s[i:i+600] else 1)

repro_reason: the refusal only shows in a git fixture whose local range holds another session's commit; the test that builds it is part of the fix, so the repro reads the message text sync prints until then
